a3302: Course home / Phase 31 · AI on Snowflake, End to End Access, Model RBAC, Cross-Region Inference and Spend Controls Lesson 31.2 60 min Lesson Completed Lesson goals What you will be able to do Grant exactly the privileges a role needs to call AI functions, specific models and agents Decide the cross-region inference setting from data-residency requirements, not by default Put budgets and per-user quotas in place before the first large job Before you start Needs : Lesson 17.30 · LLM Security: Secrets, API Key Rotation, Audit Logs and Guardrails ; Lesson 17.31 · AI Compliance: SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI-DSS, the EU AI Act and ISO 42001 Type : Lesson (setup with code). Time : about an hour. In plain words first The idea in one line Before anyone calls a model, decide who may call which model, where inference may run, and how much they may spend, and write all three down as grants and settings. The problem Brightwell's first AI pilot ran as ACCOUNTADMIN "to save time". It used the largest model for everything, inference silently ran in another region, and the month's AI bill surprised finance. All three are settings, and all three should be decided on day one. Layer 1: may this role use AI functions at all? Calling Cortex AI Functions needs two things: the account-level USE AI FUNCTIONS privilege (or a per-function USE AI FUNCTION <name> privilege) and one of two database roles. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER covers the AI functions and is also needed for Search, Analyst and Agents. SNOWFLAKE.AI_FUNCTIONS_USER is narrower: scalar AI functions only, so not AI_AGG or AI_SUMMARIZE_AGG , and not Search, Analyst, Agents or fine-tuning. Agents need SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER or SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_AGENT_USER , plus privileges on the agent and on every object its tools use. Mind the defaults: USE AI FUNCTIONS and SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX_USER are granted to PUBLIC out of the box, so every role can call AI functions until you revoke them. A governed account revokes both and grants them to named roles. Copy Layer 2: which models? Model access is now role-based. Each Cortex model has an object in SNOWFLAKE.MODELS and an application role CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-<MODEL> ; CORTEX-MODEL-ROLE-ALL covers every current and future model. The older account parameter CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST is being deprecated: from August 2026 it can only be set to 'None' , and Snowflake recommends moving to RBAC. By default, a bootstrap grant gives all models to PUBLIC ; a careful account revokes it and grants models deliberately. Copy ACCOUNTADMIN always has access, so test grants as the real role. Changes reach the Cortex REST API and AI Gateway within about five minutes. Layer 3: where may inference run? Some models are not hosted in every region. CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION (set only by ACCOUNTADMIN, at account level) decides whether a request may be processed elsewhere. Values: DISABLED ; a region group such as AWS_EU , AWS_US , AZURE_EU ; a cloud such as AWS_GLOBAL ; or ANY_REGION . Stored data stays in the account's region; the prompt and response travel encrypted and are not persisted in the processing region, and there is no egress charge. New organisations created after 9 March 2026 default to ANY_REGION , and other accounts inherit a same-cloud geography, so set it explicitly if you have residency rules. Copy Layer 4: how much may they spend? From the AI cost governance docs: budgets (monthly limits for the account or a group of objects, with notifications and actions; resource budgets for tagged agents, CoWork and Search), shared resource budgets for AI features by tagged users, and per-user quotas , the only AI control with built-in enforcement, covering AI Functions, Cortex Agents, CoCo, AI Gateway and CoWork. Budget actions can lag by hours; quotas act within minutes. A local model of the access check The decision Snowflake makes on each call can be written as a small function. Modelling it is a good way to review a grant design before applying it. Copy What you should see Copy Copy The analyst can classify and complete but not aggregate, because AI_FUNCTIONS_USER excludes the aggregate functions. The store manager cannot call AI functions directly at all, by design: they reach AI only through the agent they were granted. The second line is the residency rule doing its job: the model exists, the role could be granted it, but the account does not allow processing in the US. The answer is a different model, not a looser setting, unless the data owner agrees. (The model availability table here is invented for the exercise; check real availability with SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS .) Time : about an hour. In plain words first The idea in one line Files become usable by AI when they sit on a stage Snowflake can list, are parsed once into text with page structure, and are stored in a table that later steps can chunk, search and extract from. The problem Brightwell's knowledge lives in 3,400 files: return policies (PDF), supplier contracts (PDF and DOCX), product spec sheets (PPTX) and scanned warranty cards (JPEG). Some arrive weekly from SharePoint. Parsing every file on every run is slow and costly; parsing nothing leaves the agents blind. Stages and directory tables Copy TO_FILE('@docs.raw.files', 'policies/returns-2026.pdf') turns a staged path into a FILE reference that AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT , AI_EXTRACT , AI_COMPLETE and AI_TRANSCRIBE accept. For sources such as SharePoint and Google Drive, Openflow connectors sync files incrementally into a stage (the "simple ingest" variants) or straight into a Cortex Search service (the Cortex Search variants), optionally with document permissions. Those permissions are indexed as columns such as user_emails ; the querying application applies them by passing the user in a filter ( @contains on user_emails ), so the application must supply the right identity (lesson 31.13 ). Openflow's second generation (GA 8 Sep 2026) added more connectors (Oracle, BigQuery, Jira, HubSpot among them) and Openflow Endpoints (GA 16 Oct 2026); Snowflake Datastream (preview, announced at Summit 2026) is a managed Kafka-compatible streaming service that inherits Snowflake governance and lineage, and dynamic tables keep downstream AI tables fresh without hand-written schedules. Parsing AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT(file, options) has three modes: 'OCR' (text only), 'LAYOUT' (keeps headings and tables as Markdown) and 'AGENTIC' (adds understanding of charts and diagrams; public preview from 28 Oct 2026). Image extraction is GA (April 2026). page_split => TRUE returns one object per page, which you want for citations and chunking. It is billed per page processed, so parse once and keep the result. Copy Client-side encrypted stages also work with AI_EXTRACT and AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT since August 2026. Limits worth designing around: 100 MB per file, up to 2,000 pages per document, and page selection ( page_filter or FL_FILTER_PAGES ) to process only the pages you need, which also limits the bill. Multiply the page counts by the per-page rate in Snowflake's Service Consumption Table to turn this into credits. Time : about 65 minutes. In plain words first The idea in one line AI is only as safe and as accurate as the catalog under it: know which columns are sensitive, protect them by tag, trace every input, and publish business definitions once for every AI and BI consumer. The problem Brightwell's agents will read tickets, orders and customer tables. Nobody has a list of which columns hold personal data, masking is applied table by table when someone remembers, and "net revenue" means three different things in three dashboards. Each of these becomes an AI problem: a model sees an email it should not, or answers with the wrong revenue. Classification and tag-based masking Sensitive data classification (Enterprise Edition and above) assigns each column a semantic category (for example email or phone) and a privacy category ( IDENTIFIER , QUASI_IDENTIFIER , SENSITIVE ), recorded in the system tags SNOWFLAKE.CORE.SEMANTIC_CATEGORY and SNOWFLAKE.CORE.PRIVACY_CATEGORY . A classification profile saves the settings; associating it with a database classifies every table and view in it, and Autopilot (public preview from 26 Oct 2026) decides when to reclassify. An AI mode (public preview from 17 Aug 2026) uses a model to find more categories, at token cost. 2026 also brought semi-structured data support, EU categories, medical and health classifiers, metadata-based recommendations, and Sensitive Data Access and Entitlement reports (GA 20 Oct 2026) that show who can read and who did read sensitive columns. The payoff is tag-based masking : attach a masking policy to your own tag, map that tag to the system categories, and any newly classified email column is masked automatically, including the copies that land in AI pipelines. Copy Monitor what is covered with SYSTEM$SHOW_SENSITIVE_DATA_MONITORED_ENTITIES('DATABASE') , review results in Trust Center, and track classification credits in METERING_DAILY_HISTORY with SERVICE_TYPE = 'SENSITIVE_DATA_CLASSIFICATION' . Lineage and access history Lineage : SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE and Snowsight's lineage graph show which tables feed which; for ML, the lineage graph links source tables, feature views, datasets, models and services (lesson 31.26 ). Access history ( SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ) records which columns each query read and wrote, including queries run by AI tools on a user's behalf. With agent identity (lesson 31.30 ), actions an agent takes on a user's behalf carry the agent's identity, so the audit can tell the person from the agent acting for them. Copy Horizon Context: meaning, not only metadata Announced at Summit 2026, Horizon Context turns catalog metadata into governed business meaning that AI and BI share: definitions, relationships and calculations. In plain words first The idea in one line AI_COMPLETE is a model call that runs per row inside a query; give it a schema so every row comes back in the same shape, and check that shape before you trust it. The problem Brightwell wants every support ticket turned into a structured record: product, problem type, whether the customer asks for a refund, and urgency. Free-text answers would need parsing and would vary row to row. Structured outputs make the model return an object that matches a schema. The call AI_COMPLETE(model, prompt [, model_parameters, response_format, show_details]) . Parameters: temperature and top_p (0 to 1, default 0), max_tokens (default 4096) and guardrails (TRUE enables Cortex Guard filtering, billed as extra input tokens). response_format takes a JSON schema object whose top level is an OBJECT. Copy With show_details => TRUE , the result holds structured_output (with the object in raw_message ), created , model and usage ( prompt_tokens , completion_tokens , total_tokens , and prompt_cache_tokens when the cache was read). Model names change as Snowflake adds and retires models; check SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS and the model availability page, and pin the name in code. Copy What you should see Copy Copy The third ticket passes JSON parsing but fails the business rules: an empty product, an invented problem value and a string where a boolean belongs. A JSON schema reduces this, but your own validation decides what reaches the table. In SQL, the same checks are a CASE over the object's fields, with failures written to a review table instead of the main one. What to keep in the prompt and what not Keep Avoid The task, the allowed values, and the definition of each field Asking the model to compute totals or dates it can read from columns A short example for ambiguous fields Long instructions repeated per row when a task function would do (lesson 31.6 ) The text the model needs, nothing else Passing whole customer records "for context": cost and privacy Documents, playgrounds and model lifecycle Document intelligence : AI_COMPLETE accepts documents directly as FILE inputs (GA 2 Apr 2026), so a question about a PDF needs no separate parse step. Use AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT when you want the text for search, AI_EXTRACT for fields by schema, AI_CLASSIFY to route mixed documents, and AI_COMPLETE on the document for open questions. Playgrounds : the Cortex Playground and the Document Processing Playground (GA 22 Jan 2026) in Snowsight let you compare models and prompts on your own rows and files before writing SQL. What you can call : SHOW CORTEX BASE MODELS (GA 23 Jul 2026) lists the models available to the account. Model lifecycle : Snowflake retires models in two stages, announced in behaviour change notices. From the legacy date, accounts that never used the model cannot start; at end of life every call naming it fails. The August 2026 notice, for example, made sixteen models legacy on 12 August, with claude-4-sonnet ending on 14 October 2026. Task functions such as AI_CLASSIFY are unaffected because Snowflake manages their models. Keep model names in one configuration table or in custom AI functions (lesson 31.11 ), and re-run your evaluation when you switch. The problem Brightwell's parsed policy pages (lesson 31.3 ) are too long to retrieve whole, and splitting them badly separates a rule from its exceptions. Vectors in SQL Copy Embedding models available include snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5 (768 dimensions, English), snowflake-arctic-embed-l-v2.0 (1,024, multilingual), voyage-multilingual-2 (1,024, 32k context) and others; most have a 512-token context, so chunks longer than that are cut. Embeddings are billed on input tokens only. SPLIT_TEXT_RECURSIVE_CHARACTER(text, format, chunk_size, overlap) splits on paragraphs, then lines, then words, and in 'markdown' mode also on headings, code blocks and tables; sizes are in characters. Locally: a recursive splitter and an experiment Copy What you should see Copy Copy Tiny chunks cut rules in half, and one huge chunk always "contains" the answer but would bury it in irrelevant text and exceed embedding context limits in practice. The middle sizes, split on headings, do best. TF-IDF stands in for a neural embedding here; the method is what transfers: a fixed question set with a known answer phrase, a hit rate at k, and a sweep over chunking settings. Time : about 70 minutes. In plain words first The idea in one line A Cortex Search service keeps an always-fresh hybrid index over a query's results; you choose what is searched, what can be filtered, and how fresh it must be. The problem Brightwell's support agents need answers from policies, product manuals and 300,000 past tickets. Pure vector search misses exact product codes ("TH-2P"); pure keyword search misses paraphrases ("my tent leaks" against "water ingress"). They also need filters: only this product line, only current policies. Creating the service Copy Decisions in that statement: the search column is the chunk text; attributes are the only columns you can filter on; TARGET_LAG sets freshness (and refresh cost); the embedding model cannot be changed later without CREATE OR REPLACE (the default is snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v1.5 , English). A PRIMARY KEY (text columns) enables a cheaper refresh path, and the multi-index form ( TEXT INDEXES , VECTOR INDEXES ) lets you choose which columns are searched by keyword and which by vector, including your own embeddings. Querying Copy Copy Filter operators: @eq , @contains (arrays), @gte and @lte (numbers and dates), @primarykey , combined with @and , @or , @not . Ranking can be tuned with scoring_config : numeric_boosts (for example, popular articles), time_decays (newer tickets first) and, in multi-index services, text and vector weights; reranking is on by default. Locally: why hybrid wins A small version of what the service does: one keyword ranking (BM25), one semantic ranking, fused with reciprocal rank fusion after an attribute filter, then a reranker over the top few. The semantic side here is a stand-in for an embedding model: it maps related words to one meaning ("broke", "snapped", "break") and, like many embedding models, gives product codes little weight. Copy What you should see Copy Copy Each cell is the rank of the right document. Keyword search nails the product-code questions and fails the paraphrases ("money back for a worn tent" against "used tents are refunded"). The semantic side handles paraphrase but confuses near-identical tickets for different products (TH-2P against TR-4P). Fusion brings the right document into the top five for every question, and reranking those five with the full query puts it first. That is the design of Cortex Search: lexical and vector retrieval, fused, then reranked by default, with neural models in place of these stand-ins. Whose rights does search use? By default a Cortex Search service answers with its owner's rights: anyone who may use the service retrieves everything it indexed, and row access and masking policies on the source table do not apply at query time. Three ways to handle it: Approach How Status Index only what every user may see Build the service on a view filtered to the lowest-privileged audience; one service per audience if needed Always available Filter by permission attributes Index an attribute such as user_emails or allowed_roles and have the application pass the caller in a filter (the Openflow SharePoint pattern) Available; the application must supply the right identity Inherit source policies INHERIT_DATA_GOVERNANCE_POLICIES = TRUE plus a PRIMARY KEY ; query only with CORTEX_SEARCH_RETRIEVE or CORTEX_SEARCH_BATCH ; the REST and Python APIs and SEARCH_PREVIEW are blocked for such services; filtering happens after retrieval, so fewer results can come back Public preview 17 Nov 2026 Copy Other 2026 additions: CORTEX_SEARCH_RETRIEVE (GA 18 Nov), batch search for high-throughput jobs (GA 18 May), component scores in results (GA 4 Feb), replication (GA 14 Apr), request monitoring (preview Apr), resource budgets for search (July), auto-suspend and resume of serving (preview May), and lineage for search services (October). Restricted Session Scope: a ceiling for agent sessions A Restricted Session Scope (RSS; GA 3 Sep 2026) is a privilege ceiling that applies only while an agent is active. Know what a change costs Some AI objects cannot be altered in place. A Cortex Search service's EMBEDDING_MODEL and REFRESH_MODE are fixed at creation, so changing them means CREATE OR REPLACE , a full re-index and a short gap unless you build the new service alongside and switch. A model monitor's source and model cannot be changed after creation either (lesson 2.41 ). Agents and semantic views are cheap to replace, but every replacement is a behaviour change that needs evaluation. Copy What you should see Copy Copy The plan turns a diff into a release: the embedding-model change becomes a side-by-side build with an evaluation and a switch, the agent change is a replace gated on routing and answer tests, and the unchanged semantic view is left alone.
